items.stem: What is i⁴?
Explain why multiplying the numerator and denominator of a fraction by the conjugate of the denominator gives a real denominator.
items.answer: (c + di)(c − di) = c² + d², which is real, so the result can be written in the form x + iy.

items.stem: Explain why z + z* is always real for any complex number z.

items.stem: Explain why the least value of |z| for points on the circle |z + 4 + 5i| = 2 is 4.40.
items.answer: The nearest point of the circle to O lies on the line from O to the centre; its distance is |centre| − radius = √41 − 2 = 4.40.
items.markingKey: B1 nearest point on the line through O and the centre; B1 distance − radius [2]

items.stem: Mateo says that |z + 4i| = 1 is a circle with centre (0, 4). Explain the error.
items.answer: |z − w| is the distance from w; here w = −4i, so the centre is (0, −4), radius 1.
items.markingKey: B1 writes in the form |z − w|; B1 correct centre [2]

items.stem: Ines says that a cubic equation with real coefficients could have roots −1 + 4i, 1 + 4i and 2. Explain why this is impossible.
items.answer: Non-real roots of a polynomial with real coefficients occur in conjugate pairs, so −1 − 4i would also have to be a root, giving more than 3 roots (or the roots listed cannot all occur).
items.markingKey: B1 conjugate pairs; B1 conclusion [2]
